analysis:
Rechecked unit 0 against the replayed patches and changelog source. In .github/workflows/darkbloom-watchdog.yml:112-138,194-198, JSON aggregation moves from jq command-line arguments to files/stdin, avoiding argument-size failures without introducing executable interpretation of listing data. Pagination remains capped at 1,000 entries per listing; the changelog's "any listing size" wording does not remove that bound.
At head:238-242, rescue eligibility stops considering recent completions and the attempt's last completion. An old queued Darkbloom job can therefore trigger whole-run cancellation even while sibling jobs remain active. This expanded behavior is explicitly reflected in changelog.d/darkbloom-watchdog-listing-size.md:4-5 and docs/developer/build.md:439-449, including the possibility of mistaking intended resource-limit waits for stranded jobs. The supplied changes establish no authorization bypass, plaintext exposure, billing manipulation or artifact-integrity failure. T-043 describes a separate provider crash-recovery watchdog, not this GitHub workflow; provider controls under TB-002, TB-009, TB-011 and T-041 are not modified here.
Material integration uncertainty remains: confirm interruption/reexecution safety for affected publication or qualification jobs involving A-011/A-017, and that rerouting retains fallback labels as documented. Their implementations are not supplied, so unsafe publication or fallback failure cannot be reported as a regression. Replay is incomplete (two source units omitted); unchanged cancellation safeguards, temporary-file handling and callers could not be independently rechecked in this integration pass. No supported finding qualifies, but the cancellation contract needs further review.
